pages.title: Connecting the gear
pages.caption: A song chart tells the players what to play. It doesn’t connect a microphone or add an effect to the desk. An MCP server is a connection to gear like that: it exposes tools the agent can use. A plugin is a packaged set of additions you install. Check what’s included and what access it needs before you enable it.

pages.title: MCP server or plugin?
pages.caption: An MCP server adds tools that connect the Copilot app to a service or data source. A plugin is an installable package of skills, agents, or other capabilities. A plugin can include an MCP server, but the two aren’t interchangeable. Find both in **Customize**.

pages.title: Pack light
pages.caption: Start with the tools you already have. Add an integration only when it supplies something the task needs. Every extra tool is more noise for the agent and more access for you to review.

pages.title: A session for the chapter
pages.caption: Select **Create from** next to your course project, then **Branches**, then `main`, for a session in a new worktree. Set the mode to **Interactive**. If an agent picker appears, it should show **Default agent**. Keep the session for both exercises and the assignment. A worktree separates file changes, not installed tools.

pages.title: MCP servers
pages.caption: A browser extension can connect your browser to a service. An MCP server gives the Copilot app a connection like that, to tools and data. The server can run on your machine or at a remote service. The app can already read and search local files: use MCP when the task needs information or actions that the current tools don’t supply.

pages.title: Add the Context7 server
pages.caption: In **Customize**, select the **Browse** tab and set the type filter to **MCP**. Search for `context7`, then select **Add server**. Review the dialog: Server name `context7`, Server type `HTTP`, and the URL. Select **Add server**, then check **Installed**: **Context7** shows under **MCP Servers** with its connected icon and its enabled toggle.

pages.title: Ask out, compare at home
pages.caption: Ask Context7 only the general question about labels, and tell it not to take repository code or paths. Expand the tool activity, confirm that a **Context7** tool returned documentation, and open a source link. Then compare the guidance with the file locally, with no more external requests. The Book App’s inputs sit inside their labels, so a missing `htmlFor` isn’t a defect there.

pages.title: Plugins
pages.caption: You can add skills and MCP servers one by one, or install them as part of a plugin. A plugin can include skills, custom agents, MCP servers, or canvas extensions. A marketplace is a catalog of plugins. Read a plugin’s contents, not only the marketplace description: some start processes, call services, or run hooks.

pages.title: Find and install the plugin
pages.caption: In **Customize**, select **Browse** and set the type filter to **Plugins**. Search for `modern-web-guidance`. If nothing shows, select **Add** > **Manage marketplaces…** and confirm that **awesome-copilot** is in the **Marketplaces** list. Open the plugin’s details, compare them with its repository, then select **Install**. On **Installed** it shows under **Plugins** with its toggle on.

pages.title: Installed isn’t invoked
pages.caption: Back in your session, submit `/skills reload`, type `/` and select the `modern-web-guidance` skill (the command can carry a plugin prefix), then add the course’s prompt. Inspect the skill activity and its guide-search output. A recommendation such as `text-wrap: balance` must say what happens in browsers that don’t support it. Installation alone doesn’t prove that the skill ran.

pages.title: What Sunspire’s guild knows
pages.caption: A server supplies tools through a connected service. A plugin packages capabilities, and installing one doesn’t run them. Review what each tool can do and what data it sends. Check the tool activity and the sources, not only what the agent says. Add only what you need: a worktree doesn’t isolate installed tools.

pages.title: Your evidence table
pages.caption: In the same session, ask the default agent for a short table of both exercises: the capability used, the evidence that it ran, the source evidence, and what you learned about the Book App. Compare it with the tool activity and correct any unsupported claim. Open **Changes** and confirm it lists no changed files. Then disable only what you added, if you don’t want to keep it.

pages.title: What’s next
pages.caption: You can now connect an outside tool and use a packaged capability without mixing up installed and run. Chapter 06 keeps a session’s plan, progress and evidence in view on a canvas, starting with a community canvas installed through a plugin.

pages.title: More plugins, with care
pages.caption: After the exercise you can browse the Awesome Copilot plugin directory for other community plugins. Before you install another one, review its source, the capabilities it includes, and the access it needs.

pages.title: Where a server runs
pages.caption: Model Context Protocol defines how an AI application connects to tools and data. An MCP server supplies those tools. It can run on your machine or at a remote service. Configure MCP connections in **Customize** with the type filter set to **MCP**, not **Extensions**, and use one connection per service.

pages.title: If your organization blocks it
pages.caption: The Context7 exercise needs internet access and permission to add an MCP server. The plugin exercise needs permission to install a plugin. If your organization blocks an integration, read its example and expected output, note that you couldn’t run it, and go on with the other exercise. Neither one depends on the other.

pages.title: Can’t find MCP or plugins in Settings?
pages.caption: Use the **Customize** view in the sidebar. Labels and the commands on offer can vary by app version.

pages.title: A server is enabled but its tools fail?
pages.caption: Check the connection status, the URL, authentication, network access, and organization policy. An enabled toggle alone doesn’t prove that a server is connected. Use one connection per service. Don’t put credentials in prompts or repository files.

pages.title: A plugin is installed but its skill is missing?
pages.caption: Check the plugin’s enabled toggle and what it holds now. Run `/skills reload`, then search the `/` menu for the skill’s name, with any plugin prefix. Still missing? Wait for active work in every session to finish, quit and reopen the app, and come back to this session. Closing a window isn’t quitting.

pages.title: The agent can’t use the integration?
pages.caption: If an agent picker appears below the prompt box, confirm that it shows **Default agent**, not the read-only explainer. Then check **Tool permissions** in the mode menu, and organization policy. Don’t broaden an agent’s tools or change policy just to finish the exercise.

glossary.definition: A server that supplies tools through Model Context Protocol, so the Copilot app can reach a service or data source. It can run on your machine or at a remote service. Configure one in **Customize** with the type filter set to **MCP**.
An installable package of skills, custom agents, MCP servers, or canvas extensions. Installing a plugin is different from invoking one of the skills or agents inside it.
A catalog of plugins. In **Customize**, **Add** > **Manage marketplaces…** lists the marketplaces the app reads.
A documentation service with an MCP server. In Chapter 05 it supplies React documentation. It doesn’t become a dependency of the Book App.
